messages.subject: Re: interactions in lrm output
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

This discussion was very helpful to me for interpreting my own
results.

But something is still not totally clear to me: if you have a
significant interaction in your model, but at the same tima one of the
predictors of this interaction on its own is not significant: should
you still include this predictor in the equation (if you would write
this out) to calculate the predicted outcome?

How can I indicate the odds ratio corresponding to the coefficient of
the interaction? Should I calculate it by taking simply
exp(coefficient of the interaction) or should I adjust it by including
the coefficients of its constitutive predictors?

Thank you for your reactions!

Clara Vanderschueren, Belgium

On 24 mei, 17:48, "Stefan Th. Gries" <stgr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > But this value is true only if all other independet variables have their reference levels, isn't it?
>
> Yes.
>
> > On the other hand (tapply did'nt work with the lrm model, so I used glm)
>
> Oh yes, I meant to write glm but then you didn't mention a glm object.
>
> STG

> Stefan Th. Gries
